requirements.quote:
The first step in processing arriving response datagrams is to parse the
response.  This procedure should include:
requirements.condition: An arriving response datagram is being processed.
requirements.required_behavior: Parse the response as the first processing step.
requirements.why_checkable: The response-processing entry point and ordering of parsing relative to subsequent processing can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
The first step in processing arriving response datagrams is to parse the
response.  This procedure should include:

   - Check the header for reasonableness.  Discard datagrams which
     are queries when responses are expected.
requirements.condition: An arriving response datagram is being parsed.
requirements.required_behavior: The parsing procedure should check the header for reasonableness.
requirements.why_checkable: The phrase reasonableness supplies no concrete header acceptance criteria beyond the separately extracted query-discard rule.

requirements.quote:
The first step in processing arriving response datagrams is to parse the
response.  This procedure should include:

   - Check the header for reasonableness.  Discard datagrams which
     are queries when responses are expected.
requirements.condition: A received datagram is a query while a response is expected.
requirements.error_behavior: The parsing procedure should discard the datagram.
requirements.why_checkable: A query datagram supplied to the response-processing path can be checked for discard.

requirements.quote:
The first step in processing arriving response datagrams is to parse the
response.  This procedure should include:

   - Check the header for reasonableness.  Discard datagrams which
     are queries when responses are expected.

   - Parse the sections of the message, and insure that all RRs are
     correctly formatted.
requirements.condition: An arriving response datagram is being parsed.
requirements.required_behavior: The parsing procedure should parse the sections of the message.
requirements.why_checkable: Section parsing in the response-processing path can be inspected or exercised with section-bearing messages.

requirements.quote:
The first step in processing arriving response datagrams is to parse the
response.  This procedure should include:

   - Check the header for reasonableness.  Discard datagrams which
     are queries when responses are expected.

   - Parse the sections of the message, and insure that all RRs are
     correctly formatted.
requirements.condition: An arriving response datagram is being parsed.
requirements.required_behavior: The parsing procedure should verify that every resource record is correctly formatted.
requirements.why_checkable: The parser can be inspected for record-format validation covering every RR; this clause does not specify a particular malformed-record disposition.

requirements.quote:
- As an optional step, check the TTLs of arriving data looking
     for RRs with excessively long TTLs.  If a RR has an
     excessively long TTL, say greater than 1 week, either discard
     the whole response, or limit all TTLs in the response to 1
     week.
requirements.condition: An implementation elects to perform the optional check for excessively long TTLs in arriving response data.
requirements.required_behavior: Inspect the TTLs of arriving resource records for excessive lifetimes; greater than one week is a suggested example threshold.
requirements.why_checkable: For implementations enabling this optional policy, the TTL inspection and configured excessive-lifetime criterion can be checked; omission of the optional policy is permitted.

requirements.quote:
- As an optional step, check the TTLs of arriving data looking
     for RRs with excessively long TTLs.  If a RR has an
     excessively long TTL, say greater than 1 week, either discard
     the whole response, or limit all TTLs in the response to 1
     week.
requirements.condition: The optional long-TTL check is performed and identifies an RR with an excessively long TTL; greater than one week is an illustrative threshold.
requirements.required_behavior: Either discard the whole response or limit every TTL in that response to at most one week.
requirements.why_checkable: A response containing one RR that triggers the optional policy can be checked for whole-response discard or a one-week cap applied to all response TTLs.

requirements.quote:
The first step in processing arriving response datagrams is to parse the
response.  This procedure should include:

   - Check the header for reasonableness.  Discard datagrams which
     are queries when responses are expected.

   - Parse the sections of the message, and insure that all RRs are
     correctly formatted.

   - As an optional step, check the TTLs of arriving data looking
     for RRs with excessively long TTLs.  If a RR has an
     excessively long TTL, say greater than 1 week, either discard
     the whole response, or limit all TTLs in the response to 1
     week.

The next step is to match the response to a current resolver request.
requirements.condition: Initial parsing of an arriving response datagram has been performed.
requirements.required_behavior: Next match the response to a current resolver request.
requirements.why_checkable: The response-processing flow can be checked for correlation with a current request after parsing.

requirements.quote:
The next step is to match the response to a current resolver request.
The recommended strategy is to do a preliminary matching using the ID
field in the domain header, and then to verify that the question section
corresponds to the information currently desired.  This requires that
the transmission algorithm devote several bits of the domain ID field to
a request identifier of some sort.  This step has several fine points:
requirements.condition: The resolver is matching an arriving response to a current request.
requirements.required_behavior: The recommended strategy is to perform preliminary matching using the ID field in the domain header.
requirements.why_checkable: The response-correlation implementation can be checked for use of the domain-header ID as its recommended preliminary matching step.

requirements.quote:
The next step is to match the response to a current resolver request.
The recommended strategy is to do a preliminary matching using the ID
field in the domain header, and then to verify that the question section
corresponds to the information currently desired.  This requires that
the transmission algorithm devote several bits of the domain ID field to
a request identifier of some sort.  This step has several fine points:
requirements.condition: The resolver follows the recommended response-matching strategy and has performed preliminary matching using the domain-header ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Then verify that the question section corresponds to the information currently desired.
requirements.why_checkable: After an ID match, question-section comparison with the current request can be inspected or exercised with a mismatching question.

requirements.quote:
The next step is to match the response to a current resolver request.
The recommended strategy is to do a preliminary matching using the ID
field in the domain header, and then to verify that the question section
corresponds to the information currently desired.  This requires that
the transmission algorithm devote several bits of the domain ID field to
a request identifier of some sort.  This step has several fine points:
requirements.condition: The resolver follows the recommended ID-based response-matching strategy.
requirements.required_behavior: The transmission algorithm must devote several bits of the domain ID field to a request identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: Outgoing ID construction and request-correlation state can be inspected for allocation of multiple ID bits to request identification; the text gives no exact bit count.

requirements.quote:
- Some name servers send their responses from different
     addresses than the one used to receive the query.  That is, a
     resolver cannot rely that a response will come from the same
     address which it sent the corresponding query to.  This name
     server bug is typically encountered in UNIX systems.
requirements.condition: A resolver is matching a response to the corresponding query.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Rely on the response originating from the same address to which the corresponding query was sent.
requirements.why_checkable: Response matching can be inspected for a dependency on equality between response source address and query destination address, despite the stated possibility of different addresses.

requirements.quote:
- If the resolver retransmits a particular request to a name
     server it should be able to use a response from any of the
     transmissions.  However, if it is using the response to sample
     the round trip time to access the name server, it must be able
     to determine which transmission matches the response (and keep
     transmission times for each outgoing message), or only
     calculate round trip times based on initial transmissions.
requirements.condition: The resolver retransmits a particular request to a name server.
requirements.required_behavior: The resolver should be able to use a response from any of the transmissions of that request.
requirements.why_checkable: Responses attributable to the initial transmission and to later retransmissions can be checked for usability by the request handler.

requirements.quote:
- If the resolver retransmits a particular request to a name
     server it should be able to use a response from any of the
     transmissions.  However, if it is using the response to sample
     the round trip time to access the name server, it must be able
     to determine which transmission matches the response (and keep
     transmission times for each outgoing message), or only
     calculate round trip times based on initial transmissions.
requirements.condition: A request has been retransmitted and the resolver uses a response to sample the round-trip time to the name server.
requirements.required_behavior: Determine which transmission matches the response, or restrict round-trip-time calculations to initial transmissions.
requirements.why_checkable: The RTT sampling path can be checked for transmission attribution or an initial-transmission-only sampling policy.

requirements.quote:
- If the resolver retransmits a particular request to a name
     server it should be able to use a response from any of the
     transmissions.  However, if it is using the response to sample
     the round trip time to access the name server, it must be able
     to determine which transmission matches the response (and keep
     transmission times for each outgoing message), or only
     calculate round trip times based on initial transmissions.
requirements.condition: A request has been retransmitted and the resolver uses responses to sample the round-trip time without restricting calculations to initial transmissions.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep transmission times for each outgoing message.
requirements.why_checkable: The RTT measurement state can be inspected for a separate send time for each outgoing message when the transmission-attribution alternative is used.

requirements.quote:
- A name server will occasionally not have a current copy of a
     zone which it should have according to some NS RRs.  The
     resolver should simply remove the name server from the current
     SLIST, and continue.
requirements.condition: A name server does not have a current copy of a zone that some NS RRs indicate it should have.
requirements.required_behavior: The resolver should remove that name server from the current SLIST.
requirements.why_checkable: The resolver candidate-list state can be checked for removal of the server following this condition.

requirements.quote:
- A name server will occasionally not have a current copy of a
     zone which it should have according to some NS RRs.  The
     resolver should simply remove the name server from the current
     SLIST, and continue.
requirements.condition: A name server lacks the current zone copy indicated by some NS RRs and is removed from the current SLIST.
requirements.why_checkable: The resolver control flow can be checked for continued processing after the unavailable server is removed.
